title: Request to extend an index key to (PostCode, LastName, AddressLine1, Email)
prompt: Azure SQL Database 'RetailOps', General Purpose, 8 vCores, about 41.5 GB of memory, compatibility level 160, no readable secondary. Snapshot taken Thursday 2026-09-24 09:00 UTC. A platform failover reset the index usage counters on 2026-09-15 02:41, so they cover 9.26 days. Query Store holds data from 2026-09-11 only, because size-based cleanup has run. Month-end change freeze: 2026-09-30 18:00 to 2026-10-02 18:00. Flash sale on 2026-10-09 with a change freeze from 2026-10-08. Log rate cap: 36 MB/s. Space headroom: 213 GB.
Developer ticket: 'Extend IX_Customer_PostCode_LastName to (PostCode, LastName, AddressLine1, Email) so the fraud
check (Q13) seeks on both columns.' The missing-index DMV suggests equality PostCode, AddressLine1; include Email.

workload.sql: SELECT c.CustomerId, c.Email FROM dbo.Customer c WHERE c.PostCode = @PostCode AND c.AddressLine1 = @AddressLine1;
workload.plan: Index Seek IX_Customer_PostCode_LastName (PostCode), Key Lookup (3.1 rows on average), Filter.

facts: dbo.Customer: 4.2M rows. PostCode NVARCHAR(16), LastName NVARCHAR(200), AddressLine1 NVARCHAR(500), Email NVARCHAR(320). NVARCHAR takes 2 bytes per character.

The maximum size of a nonclustered index key is 1,700 bytes. An index whose declared key can exceed it is created with a warning; an insert or update whose key does exceed it then fails with error 1946.
PostCode: about 3.1 customers per postcode; the largest postcode has 2,940 customers. AddressLine1: 58 characters on average, 412 at most.
Q13 runs 410,000 times a day at checkout. Customer rows are written at checkout.

decisions.why: The requested key is 32 + 400 + 1,000 + 640 = 2,072 bytes, over the 1,700-byte limit. PostCode is selective, so AddressLine1 as an included column is a cheap residual check, and with Email included the key lookup goes.

must_not_create.why: The key can exceed 1,700 bytes. The index is created with a warning, and customer writes at checkout then fail.
32 + 1,000 bytes fits, but a 1,000-byte key column makes every index page hold a few rows; a residual check on about 3 rows needs no key column.
A separate index on a 1,000-byte column does not serve a predicate that always comes with PostCode.
